response:
Reviewing the document as written — I don't have file access in this session, so I haven't verified any of the cites (P0.4/P0.5-class claims) against the repo.

## Headline

The remedy has the same shape as the disease. Your own verdict is that 100% of open work went to the measuring apparatus while lever 1 produced nothing — and then the plan orders itself P0 (label the apparatus honestly), P1 (a meta-rule about measurement), P2 (five instrument decisions), P2b (the apparatus's name), P3 (the actual product), plus a new ~10pd ADOPT track to *replace the apparatus's substrate*. The single largest line item in a plan diagnosing over-investment in the lab is a lab retooling. If an outside reader saw only the section ordering, they'd reach grok's conclusion again.

Concretely: the rename, the Inspect AI swap, and #310 round 2 all outrank building-skills iter4 in the current sequence, and P3 is explicitly gated behind P1. That gate isn't load-bearing — the char-negative reshape can be built now; only the *decision to re-measure it* depends on P1. Cut the gate and move iter4 to the top.

## What's solid

- The #302 kill is the best call in the document: killing a $25 grid on a zero-cost read plus an MDE argument is real discipline, and you kept the question.
- #303 is genuine work that *closes* an issue instead of spawning two. The permutation result (cannot reject below G=6) is worth publishing as a methods limit, not just filing.
- P0 items 1–9 are all correct and cheap. Ship them.

## Three changes I'd make

**1. Re-score existing transcripts to bound the #317 contamination.** This is the deepest problem in the plan and the weakest recommendation. You note n-grams understate the coupling and that the real DV is house doctrine ("frontmatter order", "cut Background") — i.e. the judge may be rewarding what the skill teaches. Your remedy caveats it and pushes task-value outcomes to *future* benchmarks, which leaves the verdicts the README currently publishes resting on a DV you've documented as contaminated. But re-scoring is cheap: the transcripts already exist, so a task-value rubric costs judge tokens only, no generation. One re-scored benchmark gives you a bound on the contamination and either rescues or demotes the existing verdicts. Do that before any new measurement.

**2. Promote `--blind` ahead of the substrate swap.** ADR 0093 defers tell-stripping while #317 says the judge can identify arms by doctrine tells. Those two positions can't both be right. Blinding is the cheap partial defense against exactly the failure mode you just measured; it belongs on the credibility critical path, above a 10pd retooling.

**3. Scope the Inspect adoption to the judging seam, timeboxed.** Of the three cited capabilities, only multi-provider judging is on a live critical path (cross-family judge is on your bespoke-only list). Runtime dollar limits and sandboxing serve a throughput problem you don't have — last benchmark dir was 18-Jul. Spike the judging adapter (~2pd), make the full swap contingent on the G>=8 batch being actually scheduled and priced, and adopt the rule: no apparatus work over ~2pd merges until one lever-1 deliverable ships.

## Missing

- **A power caveat in the README, not just an unconverged/contaminated one.** If MDE at G=6 is ~0.35 and most skill edits are smaller than that, the honest label is "our instrument cannot detect effects below ~0.35 at affordable G." That's a bigger asterisk than P0.3's caveat and it's the one a skeptical reader will ask about.
- **A price tag on G>=8.** You killed a $25 grid but committed to a "first G>=8 batch" with no cost line. What does G=8 cost per skill, and what's the annual measurement budget? Without that, the batch is unbounded.
- **Preventive controls, or P0 regenerates next quarter.** Nine findings of one class (docs asserting what the code/practice no longer supports). Three checks kill most of it: cite-existence linting for ADR ids and repo-relative paths (catches 0.4, 0.5, 0.7); generating the README measured block from benchmark dirs instead of hand-writing it (catches 0.2, 0.3, and the retired vocabulary); a standalone-install smoke test per plugin (catches the tombstones). The generated measured block is the important one — it makes truth-in-labeling structural instead of an audit finding. It also shrinks #310 round 2, since fix-verification of #318's repairs becomes a CI job rather than a sweep class.
- **Success and stop criteria.** No exit condition anywhere. I'd propose the quarter succeeds if: one lever-1 skill ships, README claims are machine-verified, and one experiment runs whose result could have gone against you (C5 is that experiment — and notably the one comparison where the plausible effect is larger than your MDE, so it's the only well-powered thing on the list). Also make the apparatus/product commit ratio a standing metric; you already computed it once.
- **A kill criterion per bespoke component.** Five bespoke pieces justified by "nothing shipped elsewhere." Ask of each: has it changed a decision? If a survey finds nobody built it, that's ambiguous evidence — it can mean the need isn't real.

## Inconsistencies and doc hygiene

- The status header says P0 shipped and P1/0096/0097/0098 decided, but the P0/P1/P2 sections still read as open questions. A reader can't tell what's live without parsing a dense paragraph carrying eight ADR numbers. Split into a decided/shipped ledger and open work, or annotate each item with state, owner, and date.
- P3 stops "pre-reg drafting without a spend decision"; #302 starts a new C5 pre-reg. Attach the spend decision to C5 or move it.
- "6.6x" needs its interval, otherwise you've replaced one overclaim with a tighter-looking one. "~6–7x across N benchmarks" is defensible.
- The load-bearing "100% / last 10 days / 18 commits" number rests on a small window. Recompute over 90 days before enshrining it in a rebalance — if it's 60%, the remedy is a different size.
- The rename: owner-confirmed, so it's decided, but it's a mass-cite-churn event landing right after a wave of stale-cite repairs. Do it as one mechanical PR with a codemod plus the cite-existence check added *first*, so the rename can't manufacture a new P0 list.
- Your real throughput constraint is the owner: ~6 pending `/decide` calls and #321 awaiting merge. Batch all P2 decisions into one sitting with your recommendation and a default-if-no-response for each — you've already written most of the recommendations.
